results.title: Last Year, I Predicted That Alphabet Would Join the $3 Trillion Club. Here's Why the "Magnificent Seven" Stock Could Surpass $5 Trillion Before the End of 2027.
results.author: Daniel Foelber
results.description: Alphabet has surpassed $4 trillion in market capitalization, exceeding analyst predictions. The company's Gemini 3 AI model, custom TPUs, and diversified portfolio (Google Search, YouTube, Google Cloud) are driving growth. With a P/E ratio of 33.4 and projected 10-15% annual earnings growth, the stock could reach $5 trillion by end of 2027.

results.title: Alphabet Tops $4 Trillion Valuation as AI Momentum Runs Hot
results.author: Ryan Hasson
results.description: Alphabet reached a historic $4 trillion market capitalization, becoming the second-most valuable company behind NVIDIA. The milestone was driven by a landmark partnership with Apple to use Google's Gemini AI for Siri, plus Samsung's commitment to double Gemini-powered devices. Additionally, Alphabet's Wing drone delivery service expanded significantly with Walmart, planning to scale to 150+ additional stores.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Reached historic $4 trillion valuation milestone; secured major Apple partnership for Gemini AI integration; expanding Wing drone delivery business with Walmart; demonstrated ability to monetize AI at scale and defend core businesses.

results.title: Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller of Duquesne Dumped His Fund's Stake in Nvidia and Has Latched Onto a New Favorite Trillion-Dollar AI Stock
results.author: Sean Williams
results.description: Billionaire investor Stanley Druckenmiller has completely exited Duquesne Family Office's position in Nvidia, citing concerns about AI hype and potential internal competition from customers developing their own GPUs. Instead, he has been aggressively buying Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) in four of the last five quarters, viewing it as a more diversified AI play with exposure beyond just GPU manufacturing.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Druckenmiller completely exited his position despite acknowledging Nvidia's technological superiority. Concerns include AI market overhyping, potential GPU pricing power erosion from customers developing internal chips, and margin compression risks.

Druckenmiller has been consistently buying TSMC shares in four of the last five quarters. The company benefits from AI-GPU demand while maintaining diversification through CPU manufacturing, IoT solutions, and Apple supply contracts, reducing AI bubble risk.

results.title: President Donald Trump's Tax Policy Has Lit a Fire Under This Trillion-Dollar Trend That Apple, Alphabet, and Nvidia Are Taking Full Advantage Of
results.author: Sean Williams
results.description: Trump's Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which permanently reduced the corporate income tax rate from 35% to 21%, has sparked a trillion-dollar annual share buyback trend among S&P 500 companies. Apple, Alphabet, and Nvidia have been leading this trend, using their increased cash flow to repurchase their own stock rather than hiring or innovating, boosting earnings per share and stock valuations.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Apple has the most prolific share-repurchase program among S&P 500 companies, having bought back over $816 billion since 2013, reducing outstanding shares by 44% and positively impacting earnings per share and stock attractiveness.

Alphabet ranks No. 2 in share buybacks over the trailing decade with $342.4 billion in repurchases, leveraging its monopolistic position in search and growing cloud services to reward shareholders through stock buybacks.

results.title: How InterDigital Turns Its Intellectual Property Into Cold, Hard Cash
results.author: Dan Caplinger
results.description: InterDigital, an IP licensing specialist, has experienced exceptional growth by licensing its technology to major companies rather than building proprietary products. Revenue more than doubled from 2021 to 2024, net income surged from $55M to $500M, and free cash flow increased nearly sevenfold to $630M. The company has secured lucrative licensing deals with Apple, Amazon, Google, Samsung, and other tech giants, with annualized recurring revenue up nearly 50% since 2021. InterDigital has also returned $1.9B to shareholders through dividends and buybacks.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company demonstrates exceptional financial performance with revenue doubling, net income growing 9x, and free cash flow increasing 7x since 2021. Strong licensing momentum from major tech companies and successful contract renewals indicate robust business model and future growth potential.

results.title: TSMC Earnings Reset the AI Narrative After Rotation Fears Hit Tech Stocks
results.author: Jaachi Mbachu, Aciarb
results.description: TSMC reported a 35% jump in Q4 profit to NT$505.74 billion, crushing estimates with revenue hitting NT$1 trillion for the first time. The company guided for 40% Q1 revenue growth and increased capex by 37% to $52-56 billion in 2026, signaling sustained AI demand. The results reversed tech stock losses and validated the AI supply chain narrative, though tariff risks and margin pressures from overseas expansion remain concerns.
